title.zh: 卷六十八 列傳第十八: 尉遲敬德 秦叔寶 程知節 段志玄 張公謹
title.en: Volume 68 Biographies 18: Weichi Jingde, Qin Shubao, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, Zheng Gongjin
title.raw: 卷六十八 列傳第十八: 尉遲敬德 秦叔寶 程知節 段志玄 張公謹 Volume 68 Biographies 18: Weichi Jingde, Qin Shubao, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, Zheng Gongjin

sentences.zh: 尉遲敬德 秦叔寶 程知節 段志玄 張公謹 子大素 大安

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde, Qin Shubao, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, Zhang Gongjin; sons Dasu and Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde, Qin Shubao, Cheng Zhijie, Duan Zhixuan, and Zhang Gongjin; Zhang's sons Dasu and Da'an.

sentences.zh: 尉遲敬德，朔州善陽人。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jingde was a native of Shanyang in Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde came from Shanyang in Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 大業末，從軍於高陽，討捕群賊，以武勇稱，累授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign he joined the army at Gaoyang, hunted down bandit groups, was famed for martial valor, and was repeatedly appointed Chaosan dafu.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Sui, he enlisted at Gaoyang to hunt down bandits, won renown for his fighting skill, and rose repeatedly to the rank of Chaosan dafu.

sentences.zh: 劉武周起，以為偏將，與宋金剛南侵，陷晉、澮二州。

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou rose, Jingde was made a deputy general; with Song Jingang he invaded south and captured the two prefectures of Jin and Fen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou rebelled, Jingde served him as a deputy general; marching south with Song Jingang, they seized Jin and Fen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 敬德深入，至夏縣，應接呂崇茂，襲破永安王孝基，執獨孤懷恩、唐儉等。

translations.literal: Jingde pressed deep, reaching Xia County, linking with Lü Chongmao, raiding and defeating Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, and seizing Dugu Huai'en, Tang Jian, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde advanced deep into Tang territory as far as Xia County, joined forces with Lü Chongmao, routed Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, and captured Dugu Huai'en, Tang Jian, and others.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，太宗討武周於柏壁，武周令敬德與宋金剛來拒王師於介休。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, Taizong attacked Wuzhou at Baiyu; Wuzhou ordered Jingde and Song Jingang to meet the imperial army at Jiexiu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 3, when the Prince of Qin attacked Wuzhou at Baiyu, Wuzhou sent Jingde and Song Jingang to block the imperial army at Jiexiu.

sentences.zh: 金剛戰敗，奔於突厥；

translations.literal: Jingang was defeated in battle and fled to the Turks;
translations.idiomatic: Song Jingang was beaten and fled to the Turks;

sentences.zh: 敬德收其餘眾，城守介休。

translations.literal: Jingde gathered the remaining troops and held Jiexiu behind city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde rallied the survivors and defended Jiexiu behind its walls.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣任城王道宗、宇文士及往諭之。

translations.literal: Taizong sent the Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong and Yuwen Shiji to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin sent Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong and Yuwen Shiji to negotiate his surrender.

sentences.zh: 敬德與尋相舉城來降。

translations.literal: Jingde and Xun Xiang surrendered the city and came over.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde and Xun Xiang surrendered the city to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 太宗大悅，賜以曲宴，引為右一府統軍，從擊王世充於東都。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly pleased, granted him a private feast, appointed him commander of the Right First Office, and had him follow in the attack on Wang Shichong at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted, gave him a private banquet, made him commander of the Right First Office, and took him east to fight Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 既而尋相與武周下降將皆叛，諸將疑敬德必叛，囚於軍中。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Xun Xiang and the surrendered generals of Wuzhou all rebelled; the commanders suspected Jingde would surely rebel too and imprisoned him in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xun Xiang and other former Liu Wuzhou officers rebelled; the Tang generals assumed Jingde would follow and threw him in chains.

sentences.zh: 行台左僕射屈突通、尚書殷開山咸言：「敬德初歸國家，情志未附。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Executive Department Qu Tuotong and Minister Yin Kaishan both said: "Jingde has only lately submitted to the state; his feelings are not yet attached.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tuotong, left vice director of the executive department, and Yin Kaishan, a minister, both urged: "Jingde has only just come over; his loyalty is still uncertain.

sentences.zh: 此人勇健非常，縶之又久，既被猜貳，怨望必生。

translations.literal: This man is extraordinarily brave and strong; he has been bound a long time, and once doubly suspected, resentment is sure to arise.
translations.idiomatic: He is ferociously strong; kept bound this long, he will surely turn resentful once he feels we distrust him.

sentences.zh: 留之恐貽後悔，請即殺之。」

translations.literal: Keeping him may bring later regret; please kill him at once."
translations.idiomatic: If we keep him we may regret it—execute him now."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「寡人所見，有異於此。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "What I see differs from this.
translations.idiomatic: The prince replied: "I see the matter differently.

sentences.zh: 敬德若懷翻背之計，豈在尋相之後耶？」

translations.literal: If Jingde harbored a plan to turn traitor, would it come only after Xun Xiang?"
translations.idiomatic: If Jingde meant to betray us, would he have waited until after Xun Xiang rebelled?"

sentences.zh: 遽命釋之，引入臥內，賜以金寶，謂曰：「丈夫以意氣相期，勿以小疑介意。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered him released, brought him into his sleeping quarters, bestowed gold and jewels, and said: "Men pledge themselves by spirit and resolve; do not let small suspicions trouble your mind.
translations.idiomatic: He had Jingde freed at once, brought him into his private quarters, and gave him gold and gems, saying: "Men of honor trust one another's spirit; do not let petty doubts weigh on you.

sentences.zh: 寡人終不聽讒言以害忠良，公宜體之。

translations.literal: I will never heed slander to harm the loyal and worthy; you should understand this.
translations.idiomatic: I will never listen to slander against a loyal man—you must believe that.

sentences.zh: 必應欲去，今以此物相資，表一時共事之情也。」

translations.literal: If you surely wish to leave, I now use these things to support you, showing the feeling of our time working together."
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to leave, take these gifts as proof of the bond we shared in service together."

sentences.zh: 是日，因從獵於榆窠，遇王世充領步騎數萬來戰。

translations.literal: That day, while hunting at Yuke, they met Wang Shichong leading tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to battle.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, on a hunt at Yuke, Wang Shichong attacked with tens of thousands of foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 世充驍將單雄信領騎直趨太宗，敬德躍馬大呼，橫刺雄信墜馬。

translations.literal: Shichong's fierce general Shan Xiongxin led cavalry straight at Taizong; Jingde leapt his horse, shouted loudly, and thrust crosswise, knocking Xiongxin from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang's champion Shan Xiongxin charged straight at the prince; Jingde spurred forward with a shout and knocked Xiongxin from the saddle with a sideways thrust.

sentences.zh: 賊徒稍卻，敬德翼太宗以出賊圍。

translations.literal: The rebels drew back slightly; Jingde shielded Taizong and brought him out of the rebel encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fell back a little; Jingde shielded the prince and broke him out of the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 更率騎兵與世充交戰，數合，其眾大潰，擒偽將陳智略，獲排槊兵六千人。

translations.literal: He again led cavalry to fight Shichong; after several engagements the enemy force collapsed in great rout; the false general Chen Zhilüe was captured and six thousand pike-bearing soldiers were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He led the cavalry back into the fight; after several clashes Wang's army broke completely; they captured the rebel general Chen Zhilüe and six thousand pike troops.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂敬德曰：「比眾人證公必叛，天誘我意，獨保明之，福善有征，何相報之速也！」

translations.literal: Taizong said to Jingde: "Just now everyone testified you would surely rebel; Heaven guided my intent and I alone kept you clear—blessing the good has proof; how swiftly you repay!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince told him: "Everyone swore you would turn traitor; Heaven moved me to trust you alone—good deeds bring their reward, and how fast you have repaid me!"

sentences.zh: 特賜金銀一篋，此後恩眄日隆。

translations.literal: He specially bestowed a chest of gold and silver; thereafter favor and regard grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him a chest of gold and silver; from then on Jingde's favor grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 敬德善解避槊，每單騎入賊陣，賊槊攢刺，終不能傷，又能奪取賊槊，還以刺之。

translations.literal: Jingde was skilled at evading the lance; each time he entered the rebel lines alone, rebel lances thrust together yet could not harm him; he could also seize rebel lances and turn them back to stab.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde was a master of parrying the lance: riding alone into enemy ranks, he would emerge unhurt though spears thrust at him from every side, and he could seize a foe's lance and stab back with it.

sentences.zh: 是日，出入重圍，往返無礙。

translations.literal: That day he went in and out of heavy encirclements, coming and going without hindrance.
translations.idiomatic: That day he passed through ring after ring of encirclement as if unimpeded.

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉亦善馬槊，聞而輕之，欲親自試，命去槊刃，以竿相刺。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Yuanji was also skilled with the mounted lance; hearing this he belittled him and wished to test in person, ordering the lance blades removed and using poles to thrust at each other.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Li Yuanji, himself skilled with the cavalry lance, heard of this and scoffed; he wanted a personal trial and had the blades removed so they would spar with blunted poles.

sentences.zh: 敬德曰：「縱使加刃，終不能傷。

translations.literal: Jingde said: "Even if blades were added, in the end you could not harm me.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde said: "Even with real blades you still could not touch me.

sentences.zh: 請勿除之，敬德槊謹當卻刃。」

translations.literal: Please do not remove them; Jingde's lance will carefully turn the edge back."
translations.idiomatic: Leave the blades on—I will blunt mine instead."

sentences.zh: 元吉竟不能中。

translations.literal: Yuanji in the end could not strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji could not land a single hit.

sentences.zh: 太宗問曰：「奪槊、避槊，何者難易？」

translations.literal: Taizong asked: "Seizing the lance and evading the lance—which is harder or easier?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked: "Which is harder—seizing a lance or parrying one?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「奪槊難。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Seizing the lance is hard."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Seizing it is harder."

sentences.zh: 乃命敬德奪元吉槊。

translations.literal: He then ordered Jingde to seize Yuanji's lance.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jingde to disarm Yuanji in a bout.

sentences.zh: 元吉執槊躍馬，志在刺之，敬德俄頃三奪其槊。

translations.literal: Yuanji grasped his lance, leapt his horse, intent on stabbing him; in a moment Jingde thrice seized his lance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji charged with his lance set to kill; in moments Jingde stripped it from him three times running.

sentences.zh: 元吉素驍勇，雖相嘆異，甚以為恥。

translations.literal: Yuanji was by nature fierce and brave; though he marveled at him, he felt deep shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji, himself a famed fighter, was astonished but deeply humiliated.

sentences.zh: 及竇建德營於板渚，太宗將挑戰，先伏李勣、程知節、秦叔寶等兵。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande encamped at Banzhu, Taizong was about to offer battle and first hid the troops of Li Jiji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande camped at Banzhu, the prince prepared an ambush with Li Jiji, Cheng Zhijie, Qin Shubao, and others before offering battle.

sentences.zh: 太宗持弓矢，敬德執槊，造建德壘下大呼致師。

translations.literal: Taizong held bow and arrows; Jingde grasped the lance; they went to Jiande's ramparts and shouted loudly to summon battle.
translations.idiomatic: The prince took his bow while Jingde took his lance; they rode to Dou's camp and shouted a challenge.

sentences.zh: 賊眾大驚擾，出兵數千騎，太宗逡巡漸卻，前後射殺數人，敬德所殺亦十數人，遂引賊以入伏內。

translations.literal: The rebel host was greatly alarmed and disturbed; they sent out several thousand cavalry; Taizong hesitated and gradually withdrew, shooting and killing several men before and behind; those Jingde killed also numbered more than ten; thus they drew the rebels into the ambush.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels panicked and sent out thousands of horsemen; the prince feigned retreat, killing several with his bow while Jingde killed a dozen more, luring the enemy into the trap.

sentences.zh: 於是與勣等奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Jiji and the others they struck fiercely and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Then Li Jiji and the hidden force charged and smashed Dou's army.

sentences.zh: 王世充兄子偽代王琬，使於建德軍中，乘隋煬帝所御驄馬，鎧甲甚鮮，迥出軍前以誇眾。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong's nephew the false Prince of Dai Wang Wan, envoy in Jiande's army, rode the piebald horse Emperor Yang of Sui had used, his armor very bright, standing far out before the army to display pride to the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's nephew Wang Wan, the rebel Prince of Dai, was with Dou's army; he rode Emperor Yang's famous piebald stallion in gleaming armor, prancing before the lines to impress the troops.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「彼之所乘，真良馬也。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "What that one rides is truly a fine horse."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "That is a fine horse he rides."

sentences.zh: 敬德請往取之，乃與高甑生、梁建方三騎直入賊軍，擒琬，引其馬以歸，賊眾無敢當者。

translations.literal: Jingde asked to go and seize it; then with Gao Zaosheng and Liang Jianfang the three riders plunged straight into the rebel army, captured Wan, led his horse back, and none of the rebel host dared oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde volunteered to take it; with Gao Zaosheng and Liang Jianfang he charged straight into the enemy ranks, seized Wang Wan and his horse, and rode back unopposed.

sentences.zh: 又從討劉黑闥於臨洺，黑闥軍來襲李世勣，太宗勒兵掩賊，復以救之。

translations.literal: He again followed in the campaign against Liu Heita at Linming; Heita's army came to attack Li Shiji; Taizong drove troops to cover the rebels and again went to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Linming against Liu Heita; when Heita's force attacked Li Shiji, the prince moved to strike the rebels and sent Jingde to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 既而黑闥眾至，其軍四合，敬德率壯士犯圍而入，大破賊陣，太宗與江夏王道宗乘之以出。

translations.literal: Soon Heita's masses arrived and his army closed on all four sides; Jingde led stalwarts to break through the encirclement and enter, smashing the rebel formation; Taizong and the Prince of Jiangxia Li Daozong rode out on them.
translations.idiomatic: When Heita's army closed in from every side, Jingde led picked men through the ring, shattered the rebel formation, and brought the prince and Prince of Jiangxia Li Daozong out with him.

sentences.zh: 又從破徐圓朗。

translations.literal: He again followed in the defeat of Xu Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped defeat Xu Yuanlang.

sentences.zh: 累有戰功，授秦王府左二副護軍。

translations.literal: With repeated battle achievements he was appointed Left Second Deputy Protector-General of the Prince of Qin's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: After many victories he was made left second deputy protector-general of the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 隱太子、巢剌王元吉將謀害太宗，密緻書以招敬德曰：「願迂長者之眷，敦布衣之交，幸副所望也。」

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince and the Nest-stinging Prince Yuanji were about to plot harm against Taizong; they secretly sent a letter to win Jingde, saying: "We wish to divert the elder's regard and cultivate a commoner's friendship; may it fulfill what is hoped."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Li Yuanji plotted against the Prince of Qin and secretly wrote to win Jingde over: "We hope you will turn from my brother's service and befriend us as equals—may we have what we ask."

sentences.zh: 仍贈以金銀器物一車。

translations.literal: They also presented a cartload of gold, silver, and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: They sent a cartload of gold, silver, and fine goods with the letter.

sentences.zh: 敬德辭曰：「敬德起自幽賤，逢遇隋亡，天下土崩，竄身無所，久淪逆地，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Jingde declined, saying: "Jingde rose from obscure low birth; I met the fall of Sui, the realm's earth crumbling, with nowhere to hide myself; long sunk in rebel territory, my crime could not bear execution.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde refused: "I come from humble obscurity; when the Sui fell and the realm collapsed I had nowhere to turn and long served rebels—a crime that deserved death.

sentences.zh: 實荷秦王惠以生命，今又隸名籓邸，唯當以身報恩。

translations.literal: I truly owe the Prince of Qin grace in sparing my life; now again listed in the prince's mansion, I can only repay with my body.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin spared my life and took me into his household; I owe him my life and nothing else.

sentences.zh: 於殿下無功，不敢謬當重賜。

translations.literal: Toward Your Highness I have no merit and dare not wrongly accept heavy gifts.
translations.idiomatic: I have done nothing for Your Highness and dare not accept such rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 若私許殿下，便是二心，徇利忘忠，殿下亦何所用？」

translations.literal: If I privately assented to Your Highness, that would be divided loyalty, pursuing profit and forgetting faithfulness—of what use would Your Highness make me?"
translations.idiomatic: If I secretly agreed to you I would be disloyal, trading duty for gain—what use would such a man be to you?"

sentences.zh: 建成怒，是後遂絕。

translations.literal: Jiancheng was angry; thereafter they broke off.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng was furious and cut off contact with him.

sentences.zh: 敬德尋以啟聞，太宗曰：「公之素心，郁如山嶽，積金至斗，知公情不可移。

translations.literal: Jingde soon reported this to Taizong, who said: "Your constant heart is dense as mountains and hills; even gold piled to a bushel—I know your feeling cannot be moved.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde reported the offer at once; the prince said: "Your loyalty stands firm as a mountain; even a bushel of gold could not sway you—I know your heart.

sentences.zh: 送來但取，寧須慮也。

translations.literal: What they send, simply take; why need you worry?
translations.idiomatic: Take whatever they send; you need not hesitate.

sentences.zh: 若不然，恐公身不安。

translations.literal: If not, I fear your person will not be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, they may move against you personally.

sentences.zh: 且知彼陰計，足為良策。」

translations.literal: Moreover, knowing their secret plot is strategy enough."
translations.idiomatic: And learning their secret plot is strategy in itself."

sentences.zh: 元吉等深忌敬德，令壯士往刺之。

translations.literal: Yuanji and the others deeply resented Jingde and ordered stalwarts to go stab him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji and his faction hated Jingde and sent assassins after him.

sentences.zh: 敬德知其計，乃重門洞開，安臥不動，賊頻至其庭，終不敢入。

translations.literal: Jingde knew their plan; he then left his heavy gates wide open and lay at ease without moving; assassins repeatedly came to his courtyard yet in the end dared not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their intent, he left his gates wide open and slept undisturbed; the killers came to his courtyard again and again but never dared enter.

sentences.zh: 元吉乃譖敬德於高祖，下詔獄訊驗，將殺之，太宗固諫得釋。

translations.literal: Yuanji then slandered Jingde to Gaozu; an edict put him in prison for interrogation and he was to be killed; Taizong firmly remonstrated and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji denounced him to Emperor Gaozu, who had Jingde jailed for trial and execution; only the prince's desperate plea saved him.

sentences.zh: 會突厥侵擾烏城，建成舉元吉為將，密謀請太宗同送於昆明池，將加屠害。

translations.literal: When the Turks harassed Wucheng, Jiancheng nominated Yuanji as general; they secretly plotted to ask Taizong to see them off together at Kunming Pool and there add slaughter and harm.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks raided Wucheng, Jiancheng named Yuanji commander and secretly planned to invite the prince to see them off at Kunming Pool and murder him there.

sentences.zh: 敬德聞其謀，與長孫無忌遽啟太宗曰：「大王若不速正之，則恐被其所害，社稷危矣。」

translations.literal: Jingde heard their plot; with Zhangsun Wuji he urgently reported to Taizong: "If the King does not quickly set things right, I fear you will be harmed by them and the altars of state will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Jingde learned of the plot and with Zhangsun Wuji urged the prince: "If you do not act at once, they will kill you and the realm will be lost."

sentences.zh: 太宗嘆曰：「今二宮離阻骨肉，滅棄君親，危亡之機，共所知委。

translations.literal: Taizong sighed: "Now the two palaces estrange flesh and bone, destroy and abandon ruler and kin; the moment of peril and ruin is what all know and entrust.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sighed: "My brothers have turned against kin and king; the danger is plain to everyone.

sentences.zh: 寡人雖深被猜忌，禍在須臾，然同氣之情，終所未忍。

translations.literal: Though I am deeply suspected and disaster hangs in an instant, yet the feeling of shared breath I have never yet been able to bear away.
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply suspected and death is near, yet I still cannot bring myself to harm my own brothers.

sentences.zh: 欲待其先起，然後以義討之，公意以為何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to wait until they rise first, then with righteousness punish them—what does your view think?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to wait until they strike first, then move against them with justice—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 敬德曰：「人情畏死，眾人以死奉王，此天授也。

translations.literal: Jingde said: "Human nature fears death; the masses offer death to serve the King—this is Heaven's grant.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde said: "Men fear death, yet these men are ready to die for you—that is Heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 若天與不取，反受其咎。

translations.literal: If Heaven grants and you do not take, you will instead receive its blame.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven offers and you refuse, you will answer for it.

sentences.zh: 雖存仁愛之小情，忘社稷之大計，禍至而不恐，將亡而自安，失人臣臨難不避之節，乏先賢大義滅親之事，非所聞也。

translations.literal: Though you keep small feeling of benevolence and love, you forget the great plan of the altars of state; when disaster comes you are not afraid, about to perish yet self-assured—you lose a minister's integrity of not avoiding hardship, lack the former sages' great righteousness in extinguishing kin—this is not what I have heard.
translations.idiomatic: To cherish private affection while forgetting the realm, to face ruin without fear, to neglect a subject's duty to meet peril head-on, to lack the sages' willingness to sacrifice kin for the state—such things I have never heard praised.

sentences.zh: 以臣愚誠，請先誅之。

translations.literal: With this subject's foolish sincerity, I ask to execute them first.
translations.idiomatic: In all sincerity, I beg you to strike first.

sentences.zh: 王若不從，敬德言請奔逃亡命，不能交手受戮。

translations.literal: If the King does not follow, Jingde says he asks to flee and save his life; he cannot meet blades and receive slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: If you refuse, I must flee for my life—I will not stay to be butchered.

sentences.zh: 且因敗成功，明賢之高見；

translations.literal: Moreover, turning defeat into success is the lofty view of the bright and worthy;
translations.idiomatic: To turn defeat into victory is the mark of a sage;

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福，智士之先機。

translations.literal: turning calamity into blessing is the wise man's foresight.
translations.idiomatic: to turn disaster into blessing is the wise man's foresight.

sentences.zh: 敬德今若逃亡，無忌亦欲同去。」

translations.literal: If Jingde now flees, Wuji also wishes to go together."
translations.idiomatic: If I run, Wuji means to run with me."

sentences.zh: 太宗猶豫未決，無忌曰：「王今不從敬德之言，必知敬德等非王所有。

translations.literal: Taizong hesitated and could not decide; Wuji said: "If the King now does not follow Jingde's words, you must know that Jingde and the others are not the King's to keep.
translations.idiomatic: The prince still wavered; Wuji said: "If you reject Jingde now, you will lose him and all of us with him.

sentences.zh: 事今敗矣，其若之何？」

translations.literal: The affair is now ruined—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The cause is lost—what then?"

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「寡人所言，未可全棄，公更圖之。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "What I have said cannot be wholly abandoned; you should plot further."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "Do not abandon my plan entirely—find another way."

sentences.zh: 敬德曰：「王今處事有疑，非智；

translations.literal: Jingde said: "The King now handles affairs with doubt—that is not wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: Jingde said: "Hesitation in crisis is not wisdom;

sentences.zh: 臨難不決，非勇。

translations.literal: facing hardship without decision—that is not courage.
translations.idiomatic: indecision before danger is not courage.

sentences.zh: 王縱不從敬德言，請自決計，其如家國何？

translations.literal: Even if the King does not follow Jingde's words, please decide for yourself—what of family and state?
translations.idiomatic: Even if you reject my counsel, decide for yourself—what of the realm and your house?

sentences.zh: 其如身命何？

translations.literal: What of your person and life?
translations.idiomatic: What of your own life?

sentences.zh: 且在外勇士八百餘人，今悉入宮，控弦被甲，事勢已就，王何得辭！」

translations.literal: Moreover, more than eight hundred stalwarts outside—now all have entered the palace, drawn bowstrings and donned armor; the situation is already set—how can the King decline!"
translations.idiomatic: More than eight hundred armed men are already in the palace with bows drawn and armor on—the deed is ready; you cannot refuse!"

sentences.zh: 敬德又與侯君集日夜進勸，然後計定。

translations.literal: Jingde again with Hou Junji day and night urged forward; only then was the plan settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde and Hou Junji pressed him day and night until the plan was fixed.

sentences.zh: 時房玄齡、杜如晦皆被高祖斥出秦府，不得復入。

translations.literal: At that time Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had both been expelled by Gaozu from the Prince of Qin's mansion and could not re-enter.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had been banished from the prince's household by the emperor and could not return.

sentences.zh: 太宗令長孫無忌密召之，玄齡等報曰：「有敕不許更事王，今若私謁，必至誅滅，不敢奉命。」

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Zhangsun Wuji to summon them secretly; Xuanling and the others replied: "There is an edict forbidding us to serve the King again; if we now visit privately, we will surely reach execution and extinction—we dare not obey the command."
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent Zhangsun Wuji to fetch them secretly; they replied: "We are forbidden to serve you again; a private visit would mean death—we dare not come."

sentences.zh: 太宗大怒，謂敬德曰：「玄齡、如晦豈背我耶？」

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly angry and said to Jingde: "Would Xuanling and Ruhui betray me?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince flew into a rage and told Jingde: "Would Fang and Du betray me?"

sentences.zh: 取所佩刀授敬德曰：「公且往，觀其無來心，可並斬其首持來也。」

translations.literal: He took the sword at his belt and gave it to Jingde, saying: "Sir, go for now; if you see they have no mind to come, you may together cut off their heads and bring them."
translations.idiomatic: He handed Jingde his own sword: "Go. If they will not come, cut off their heads and bring them here."

sentences.zh: 敬德又與無忌喻曰：「王已決計剋日平賊，公宜即入籌之。

translations.literal: Jingde again with Wuji instructed them: "The King has already decided the day to pacify the rebels; you gentlemen should enter at once to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde told them through Wuji: "The prince has set the day to strike; come at once to plan with us.

sentences.zh: 我等四人不宜群行在道。」

translations.literal: We four should not travel the road in a group."
translations.idiomatic: The four of us must not travel together on the road."

sentences.zh: 於是玄齡、如晦著道士服隨無忌入，敬德別道亦至。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuanling and Ruhui wore Taoist robes and followed Wuji in; Jingde by another route also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Du entered in Taoist dress with Wuji; Jingde came by another route.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，建成既死，敬德領七十騎躡踵繼至，元吉走馬東奔，左右射之墜馬。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month, after Jiancheng was already dead, Jingde led seventy riders treading on his heels in pursuit; Yuanji spurred his horse fleeing east; those left and right shot him and he fell from his horse.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month, after Jiancheng was killed, Jingde pursued with seventy horsemen; Yuanji fled east and was shot from the saddle by the prince's men.

sentences.zh: 太宗所乘馬又逸於林下，橫被所繣，墜不能興。

translations.literal: Taizong's mount again bolted into the woods below; it was caught crosswise by what tethered it and fell, unable to rise.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's horse bolted into the woods, caught on a vine, and threw him; he could not get up.

sentences.zh: 元吉遽來奪弓，垂欲相扼，敬德躍馬叱之，於是步走，欲歸武德殿，敬德奔逐射殺之。

translations.literal: Yuanji hurried to seize the bow; about to throttle each other, Jingde leapt his horse and shouted at him; Yuanji then walked on foot, wishing to return to Wude Hall; Jingde ran in pursuit and shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji rushed to seize the bow and nearly throttled the prince; Jingde spurred up shouting; Yuanji fled on foot toward Wude Hall and Jingde overtook and shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 其宮府諸將薛萬徹、謝叔方、馮立等率兵大至，屯於玄武門，殺屯營將軍。

translations.literal: The generals of their palaces Xue Wanche, Xie Shufang, Feng Li, and others led troops in great numbers arriving, encamped at Xuanwu Gate, and killed the garrison camp general.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng's generals Xue Wanche, Xie Shufang, Feng Li, and others marched up in force to Xuanwu Gate and killed the garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 敬德持建成、元吉首以示之，宮府兵遂散。

translations.literal: Jingde held the heads of Jiancheng and Yuanji to show them; the palace troops thereupon dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde displayed the brothers' heads; the Eastern Palace troops scattered.

sentences.zh: 是時，高祖泛舟於海池。

translations.literal: At that time Gaozu was boating on the Sea Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Emperor Gaozu was boating on the imperial pond.

sentences.zh: 太宗命敬德侍衛高祖。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Jingde to attend and guard Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent Jingde to guard the emperor.

sentences.zh: 敬德擐甲持矛，直至高祖所。

translations.literal: Jingde donned armor and grasped spear, going straight to where Gaozu was.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde strode to the emperor in full armor with spear in hand.

sentences.zh: 高祖大驚，問曰：「今日作亂是誰？

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly startled and asked: "Who is making trouble today?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and demanded: "Who has risen in revolt today?

sentences.zh: 卿來此何也？」

translations.literal: Why have you come here?
translations.idiomatic: Why have you come here like this?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「秦王以太子、齊王作亂，舉兵誅之，恐陛下驚動，遣臣來宿衛。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The Prince of Qin, because the Crown Prince and Prince of Qi made rebellion, raised troops to execute them; fearing Your Majesty would be alarmed, he sent me to guard overnight."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "The Prince of Qin has put down a revolt by the crown prince and Prince of Qi. Fearing Your Majesty might be alarmed, he sent me to guard you."

sentences.zh: 高祖意乃安。

translations.literal: Gaozu's mind then grew calm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's fears subsided.

sentences.zh: 南衙、北門兵馬及二宮左右猶相拒戰，敬德奏請降手敕，令諸軍兵並受秦王處分，於是內外遂定。

translations.literal: The troops of the Southern Yamen, Northern Gate, and the two palaces' attendants still opposed each other in battle; Jingde memorialized asking for a handwritten edict to be issued, ordering all armies to accept the Prince of Qin's disposition; thus inside and outside were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting still raged between palace guards and Eastern Palace forces; Jingde obtained an imperial order placing all troops under the prince's command, and the realm was pacified.

sentences.zh: 高祖勞敬德曰：「卿於國有安社稷之功。」

translations.literal: Gaozu comforted Jingde, saying: "You have the achievement of securing the altars of state for the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him: "You have saved the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 賜珍物甚眾。

translations.literal: He bestowed many precious things.
translations.idiomatic: He showered him with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 太宗升春宮，授太子左衛率。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the Eastern Palace, he appointed him Left Guard Commander of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became heir apparent, he made Jingde commander of the crown prince's left guard.

sentences.zh: 時議者以建成等左右百餘人，併合從坐籍沒，唯敬德執之不聽，曰：「為罪者二凶，今已誅訖，若更及支黨，非取安之策。」

translations.literal: At the time debaters held that Jiancheng's attendants, more than a hundred, should together be implicated and their property confiscated; only Jingde held to it and would not listen, saying: "Those guilty are the two villains, now already executed; if we extend further to branches and factions, that is not a policy to secure peace."
translations.idiomatic: Many urged that Jiancheng's hundred-odd followers be punished and their property seized; Jingde alone objected: "Only the two culprits deserved death; to punish their whole circle is no way to secure peace.

sentences.zh: 由是獲免。

translations.literal: Through this they obtained exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to him they were spared.

sentences.zh: 及論功，敬德與長孫無忌為第一，各賜絹萬匹；

translations.literal: When merits were discussed, Jingde and Zhangsun Wuji ranked first, each granted ten thousand bolts of silk;
translations.idiomatic: In the distribution of rewards Jingde and Zhangsun Wuji ranked first, each receiving ten thousand bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 齊王府財幣器物，封其全邸，盡賜敬德。

translations.literal: the wealth, currency, and vessels of the Prince of Qi's mansion were sealed in its whole residence and entirely bestowed on Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: and the entire treasury of Prince of Qi Li Yuanji's mansion was sealed and given to Jingde.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，拜右武候大將軍，賜爵吳國公，與長孫無忌、房玄齡、杜如晦四人並食實封千三百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Right Martial Guard Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Wu, and with Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui the four together received substantive fiefs of thirteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 he became right martial guard grand general and Duke of Wu; he and Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui each held substantive fiefs of 1,300 households.

sentences.zh: 會突厥來入寇，授涇州道行軍總管以擊之。

translations.literal: When the Turks came to invade, he was appointed Commander on Campaign of the Jingzhou Circuit to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: When Turks invaded, he was made commander on campaign of the Jingzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 賊至涇陽，敬德輕騎與之挑戰，殺其名將，賊遂敗。

translations.literal: The rebels reached Jingyang; Jingde with light cavalry challenged them in battle, killed their famed general, and the rebels were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingyang he met them with light cavalry, killed their champion, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 敬德好訐直，負其功，每見無忌、玄齡、如晦等短長，必面折廷辯，由是與執政不平。

translations.literal: Jingde loved blunt straightness and relied on his achievements; whenever he saw Wuji, Xuanling, Ruhui, and others' faults and merits, he would invariably face them down in court debate; thus he was at odds with those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde was blunt and proud of his merit; he openly quarreled with Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui in court and fell out with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 三年，出為襄州都督。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as Military Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he was posted as military governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，累遷同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By year 8 he had risen to governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴慶善宮，時有班在其上者，敬德怒曰：「汝有何功，合坐我上？」

translations.literal: Once while attending a feast at Qingshan Palace, when someone of lower rank sat above him, Jingde angrily said: "What achievement have you, that you should sit above me?"
translations.idiomatic: At a feast in Qingshan Palace he flew into a rage when a man of lower rank sat above him: "What have you done to rank above me?

sentences.zh: 任城王道宗次其下，因解喻之。

translations.literal: Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong was ranked below him and therefore explained and admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Rencheng Li Daozong, seated below, tried to calm him.

sentences.zh: 敬德勃然，拳毆道宗目，幾至眇。

translations.literal: Jingde erupted and with his fist struck Daozong in the eye, nearly blinding him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde struck Daozong in the eye and nearly blinded him.

sentences.zh: 太宗不懌而罷，謂敬德曰：「朕覽漢史，見高祖功臣獲全者少，意常尤之。

translations.literal: Taizong was displeased and ended the feast; he said to Jingde: "I have read Han history and see that few of Gaozu's meritorious ministers were preserved whole—I have often blamed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ended the feast in displeasure and told Jingde: "Reading Han history, I have long regretted how few of Gaozu's meritorious followers died in peace.

sentences.zh: 及居大位以來，常欲保全功臣，令子孫無絕。

translations.literal: Since occupying the great position I have often wished to preserve meritorious ministers and let their descendants not be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking the throne I have wanted to keep my meritorious men alive and their lines unbroken.

sentences.zh: 然卿居官輒犯憲法，方知韓、彭夷戮，非漢祖之愆。

translations.literal: Yet you in office repeatedly violate the statutes; only then do I know Han Xin and Peng Yue's extermination was not Han Gaozu's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you break the law again and again—I see now that Han Xin and Peng Yue were not killed without cause.

sentences.zh: 國家大事，唯賞與罰，非分之恩，不可數行，勉自修飭，無貽後悔也。」

translations.literal: The great affairs of state rely only on reward and punishment; undue favor cannot be repeatedly granted—strive to discipline yourself and bring no later regret."
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on reward and punishment alone; favor beyond merit cannot be granted often—mend your ways before you regret it.

sentences.zh: 十一年，封建功臣為代襲刺史，冊拜敬德宣州刺史，改封鄂國公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year meritorious ministers were enfeoffed as hereditary prefects; Jingde was appointed by patent as Prefect of Xuanzhou and his fief changed to Duke of E.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was enfeoffed as hereditary prefect of Xuanzhou and made Duke of E.

sentences.zh: 後歷鄜、夏二州都督。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Military Governor of Fu and Xia prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Fu and Xia prefectures.

sentences.zh: 十七年，抗表乞骸骨，授開府儀同三司，令朝朔望。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he submitted a memorial resisting and begging to retire; he was granted Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon of the First Order, and ordered to attend court on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he petitioned to retire and was made grand master of the palace with gold seal, attending court on the first and fifteenth.

sentences.zh: 尋與長孫無忌等二十四人圖形於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: Soon he and Zhangsun Wuji and twenty-two others had their portraits painted at Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was among the twenty-four men portrayed at Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 及太宗將征高麗，敬德奏言：「車駕若自往遼左，皇太子又在定州，東西二京，府庫所在，雖有鎮守，終是空虛。

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to campaign against Goryeo, Jingde memorialized: "If the imperial carriage goes in person to Liaodong, and the crown prince is again at Dingzhou, the eastern and western capitals where the treasuries lie—though there are garrisons, in the end they are empty.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to invade Goryeo, Jingde warned: "If Your Majesty goes to Liaodong while the crown prince is at Dingzhou, the two capitals where the treasuries lie will be left dangerously thin despite garrisons.

sentences.zh: 遼東路遙，恐有玄感之變。

translations.literal: The road to Liaodong is far; I fear there may be a change like Xuan Gan's.
translations.idiomatic: The long march east invites a rebellion like Yang Xuangan's.

sentences.zh: 且邊隅小國，不足親勞萬乘，伏請委之良將，自可應時摧滅。」

translations.literal: Moreover a small state on the border fringe is not worth the ten-thousand-chariot ruler laboring in person; I humbly ask to entrust it to good generals, who of themselves can destroy it in season."
translations.idiomatic: This petty border kingdom is not worth the Son of Heaven's personal labor—send able generals and they will crush it in due course.

sentences.zh: 太宗不納，令以本官行太常卿，為左一馬軍總管，從破高麗於駐蹕山。

translations.literal: Taizong did not accept it; he ordered him to act as Grand Master of Ceremonies in his regular office, as Left First Cavalry Commander, following to defeat Goryeo at Zhubeishan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and made him acting grand master of ceremonies and left first cavalry commander on the campaign that defeated Goryeo at Zhubeishan.

sentences.zh: 軍還，依舊致仕。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he resumed retirement as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign he retired again.

sentences.zh: 敬德末年篤信仙方，飛煉金石，服食雲母粉，穿築池台，崇飾羅綺，嘗奏清商樂以自奉養，不與外人交通，凡十六年。

translations.literal: In Jingde's later years he devoutly believed immortal formulas, smelted metal and stone, ingested powdered mica, built pools and terraces, adorned himself with brocades, once presented pure Shang music to nourish himself, and did not interact with outsiders—for sixteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years he pursued alchemy, took mica powder, built lavish gardens, lived in luxury, played court music for his own pleasure, and shunned visitors for sixteen years.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年，高宗以敬德功，追贈其父為幽州都督。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing, Emperor Gaozong because of Jingde's merit posthumously enfeoffed his father as Military Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 3 Emperor Gaozong enfeoffed his father posthumously as military governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 其年薨，年七十四。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日，令京官五品以上及朝集使赴宅哭，冊贈司徒、并州都督，謚曰忠武，賜東園秘器，陪葬於昭陵。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong held mourning for him, suspended court for three days, ordered capital officials of the fifth rank and above and tribute envoys to go to his residence to weep; by patent he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works and Military Governor of Bingzhou, posthumous name Zhongwu, bestowed eastern-garden secret vessels, and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong mourned him, closed court three days, ordered officials of the fifth rank and above and tribute envoys to attend his funeral, and posthumously made him minister of works and military governor of Bingzhou with the posthumous name Loyal and Martial; he was buried at Zhaoling with imperial funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 子寶琳嗣，官至衛尉卿。

translations.literal: His son Baolin inherited, reaching the office of Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baolin succeeded him and rose to commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 秦叔寶，名瓊，齊州歷城人。

translations.literal: Qin Shubao, personal name Qiong, was a native of Licheng in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shubao, whose name was Qiong, came from Licheng in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為隋將來護兒帳內。

translations.literal: In the Daye reign he served in the tent retinue of the Sui general Lai Hu'er.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui he served in the guard of the general Lai Hu'er.

sentences.zh: 叔寶喪母，護兒遣使吊之，軍吏怪曰：「士卒死亡及遭喪者多矣，將軍未嘗降問，獨吊叔寶何也？」

translations.literal: When Shubao's mother died, Hu'er sent an envoy to condole; the army officers wondered: "Among soldiers many die or suffer bereavement—why has the general never lowered inquiry except to condole Shubao?
translations.idiomatic: When Shubao's mother died, Lai Hu'er sent condolences; his officers asked why he singled out Shubao among so many bereaved soldiers.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「此人勇悍，加有志節，必當自取富貴，豈得以卑賤處之？」

translations.literal: He replied: "This man is brave and fierce, and moreover has will and integrity; he will surely win wealth and honor for himself—how can one treat him as base and lowly?
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "This man is brave and has true spirit; he will rise to wealth and honor—do not treat him as a common soldier."

sentences.zh: 隋末群盜起，從通守張須陀擊賊帥盧明月於下邳。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui bandits rose everywhere; he followed Defender-in-chief Zhang Xuantuo to strike the bandit chief Lu Mingyue at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion spread at the end of the Sui, he followed Zhang Xuantuo against the rebel Lu Mingyue at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 賊眾十餘萬，須陀所統才萬人，力勢不敵，去賊六七里立柵，相持十餘日，糧盡將退，謂諸將士曰：「賊見兵卻，必輕來追我。

translations.literal: The rebel host was more than a hundred thousand; what Xuantuo commanded was only ten thousand men; strength and momentum could not match; they left the rebels six or seven li and set up palisades, facing off more than ten days; provisions exhausted, about to withdraw; he said to the officers and soldiers: "When the rebels see the army retreat, they will surely come lightly to pursue us.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels numbered over 100,000 against Xuantuo's 10,000; after ten days' stalemate with food running out, he told his men: "When they see us withdraw they will pursue lightly.

sentences.zh: 其眾既出，營內即虛，若以千人襲營，可有大利。

translations.literal: Once their masses have come out, the camp within is empty; if a thousand men raid the camp, there can be great profit.
translations.idiomatic: Their camp will be empty—if a thousand men strike it, we can win greatly.

sentences.zh: 此誠危險，誰能去者？」

translations.literal: This is truly dangerous—who can go?
translations.idiomatic: It is dangerous—who will go?

sentences.zh: 人皆莫對，唯叔寶與羅士信請行。

translations.literal: No one answered; only Shubao and Luo Shixin asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: No one spoke until Shubao and Luo Shixin volunteered.

sentences.zh: 於是須陀委柵遁，使二人分領千兵伏於蘆葦間。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuantuo abandoned the palisade and fled, sending the two to command a thousand men each in ambush among the reeds.
translations.idiomatic: Xuantuo withdrew, leaving them each with 1,000 men hidden in the reeds.

sentences.zh: 既而明月果悉兵追之，叔寶與士信馳至其柵，柵門閉不得入，二人超升其樓，拔賊旗幟，各殺數人，營中大亂。

translations.literal: Soon Mingyue as expected led all his troops in pursuit; Shubao and Shixin galloped to his palisade; the gate was closed and they could not enter; the two leapt onto its tower, pulled down rebel banners, each killed several men, and the camp fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue pursued with his whole army; the two galloped to his camp, scaled the gate tower when the gates closed, tore down his banners, killed several men, and threw the camp into chaos.

sentences.zh: 叔寶、士信又斬關以納外兵，因縱火焚其三十餘柵，煙焰漲天。

translations.literal: Shubao and Shixin again cut through the gate to admit outside troops, and set fire burning more than thirty palisades; smoke and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: They broke the gate for the main force and burned more than thirty stockades until the sky was black with smoke.

sentences.zh: 明月奔還，須陀又回軍奮擊，大破賊眾。

translations.literal: Mingyue ran back; Xuantuo turned the army and struck fiercely, routing the rebel host utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue fled back; Xuantuo counterattacked and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 明月以數百騎遁去，余皆虜之。

translations.literal: Mingyue escaped with several hundred cavalry; the rest were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue escaped with a few hundred horsemen; the rest were captured.

sentences.zh: 由是勇氣聞於遠近。

translations.literal: Thus his courage was heard far and near.
translations.idiomatic: His fame for courage spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 又擊孫宣雅於海曲，先登破之。

translations.literal: He again struck Sun Xuanya at Haiqu, taking the lead in the assault and breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: He again led the assault that broke Sun Xuanya at Haiqu.

sentences.zh: 以前後累勳授建節尉。

translations.literal: For accumulated merits before and after he was appointed Jianjie wei.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated merit he was made a Jianjie commandant.

sentences.zh: 從須陀進擊李密於滎陽，軍敗，須陀死之，叔寶以餘眾附裴仁基。

translations.literal: Following Xuantuo he advanced to strike Li Mi at Xingyang; the army was defeated and Xuantuo died; Shubao with the remaining troops attached to Pei Renji.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xuantuo against Li Mi at Xingyang; when Xuantuo was killed, Shubao joined Pei Renji.

sentences.zh: 會仁基以武牢降於李密，密得叔寶大喜，以為帳內驃騎，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: When Renji surrendered Wulao to Li Mi, Mi gained Shubao and was greatly pleased, making him tent-retinue Flying Cavalry general and treating him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Renji surrendered Wulao to Li Mi, Mi was delighted and made Shubao a flying-cavalry general in his guard, treating him generously.

sentences.zh: 密與化及大戰於黎陽童山，為流矢所中，墮馬悶絕。

translations.literal: Mi fought a great battle with Yu Huaji at Tongshan in Liyang and was struck by a stray arrow; he fell from his horse and lost consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: In a great battle with Yu Huaji at Tongshan in Liyang, Mi was struck by a stray arrow and fell unconscious from his horse.

sentences.zh: 左右奔散，追兵且至，唯叔寶獨捍衛之，密遂獲免。

translations.literal: Those left and right scattered in flight; pursuing troops were about to arrive; only Shubao alone defended him, and Mi thus escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: His guards fled; pursuers were closing in; only Shubao defended him until Mi was safe.

sentences.zh: 叔寶又收兵與之力戰，化及乃退。

translations.literal: Shubao again gathered troops and fought with him with force; Huaji then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao rallied troops and fought Yu Huaji off.

sentences.zh: 後密敗，又為王世充所得，署龍驤大將軍。

translations.literal: Later when Mi was defeated, he again came into Wang Shichong's possession and was appointed Dragon-soaring Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After Mi's defeat Wang Shichong took him and made him dragon-soaring grand general.

sentences.zh: 叔寶薄世充之多詐，因其出抗官軍，至於九曲，與程咬金、吳黑闥、牛進達等數十騎西馳百許步，下馬拜世充曰：「雖蒙殊禮，不能仰事，請從此辭。」

translations.literal: Shubao despised Shichong's much deceit; when Shichong went out to resist the imperial army, reaching Jiugqu, with Cheng Yaojin, Wu Heita, Niu Jinda, and several tens of riders he galloped west more than a hundred paces, dismounted and bowed to Shichong: "Though I have received extraordinary favor, I cannot serve you with head raised—please let me take leave from here.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao despised Shichong's deceit; at Jiugqu, with Cheng Yaojin, Wu Heita, Niu Jinda, and dozens of riders, he rode west, dismounted, and said: "Though you have honored me, I cannot serve you— I take my leave.

sentences.zh: 世充不敢逼，於是來降。

translations.literal: Shichong did not dare press them; thus they came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong did not dare stop them, and they defected to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 高祖令事秦府，太宗素聞其勇，厚加禮遇。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered him to serve the Prince of Qin's mansion; Taizong had long heard of his courage and treated him with thick courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu assigned him to the Prince of Qin; the prince, knowing his fame, honored him richly.

sentences.zh: 從鎮長春宮，拜馬軍總管。

translations.literal: He followed in garrisoning Changchun Palace and was appointed Cavalry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Changchun Palace as cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 又從征於美良川，破尉遲敬德，功最居多。

translations.literal: He again followed on campaign at Meiliang River, defeating Yuchi Jingde, his achievements ranking the most.
translations.idiomatic: At Meiliang River he defeated Yuchi Jingde and won the greatest credit.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使賜以金瓶，勞之曰：「卿不顧妻子，遠來投我，又立功效。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent an envoy bestowing a golden bottle and comforted him: "You disregarded wife and children, came from afar to join me, and again established achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent a golden bottle and said: "You left your family to join me from afar and have served brilliantly.

sentences.zh: 朕肉可為卿用者，當割以賜卿，況子女玉帛乎？

translations.literal: Flesh of my body that can be used for you—I would cut and bestow it; how much more sons and daughters, jade, and silk?
translations.idiomatic: If my own flesh could help you I would cut it off for you—how much more mere wealth?

sentences.zh: 卿當勉之。」

translations.literal: You should strive hard.
translations.idiomatic: Press on.

sentences.zh: 尋授秦王右三統軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed the Prince of Qin's Right Third Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made the prince's right third commander.

sentences.zh: 又從破宋金剛於介休。

translations.literal: He again followed in defeating Song Jingang at Jiexiu.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat Song Jingang at Jiexiu.

sentences.zh: 錄前後勳，賜黃金百斤、雜彩六千段，授上柱國。

translations.literal: Recording merits before and after, he was granted a hundred jin of gold and six thousand lengths of mixed silks, and appointed Supreme Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: For his cumulative merit he received a hundred jin of gold, six thousand lengths of silk, and the title supreme pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 從討王世充，每為前鋒。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Wang Shichong, he was always in the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the war on Wang Shichong he always led the van.

sentences.zh: 太宗將拒竇建德於武牢，叔寶以精騎數十先陷其陣。

translations.literal: When Taizong was about to resist Dou Jiande at Hulao, Shubao with several tens of elite cavalry first broke their formation.
translations.idiomatic: At Hulao he led several dozen elite horsemen in the first charge that broke Dou Jiande's line.

sentences.zh: 世充平，進封翼國公，賜黃金百斤、帛七千段。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, he was advanced to Duke of Yi, granted a hundred jin of gold and seven thousand lengths of silk.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichong's fall he was made Duke of Yi with a hundred jin of gold and seven thousand lengths of silk.

sentences.zh: 從平劉黑闥，賞物千段。

translations.literal: Following the pacification of Liu Heita, he was rewarded with a thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: For Liu Heita's defeat he received a thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 叔寶每從太宗征伐，敵中有驍將銳卒，炫耀人馬，出入來去者，太宗頗怒之，輒命叔寶往取。

translations.literal: Whenever Shubao followed Taizong on campaign, if among the enemy there were fierce generals and sharp soldiers who displayed men and horses, coming and going, Taizong was often angered and would order Shubao to go take them.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign, whenever enemy champions paraded before the lines, the prince would send Shubao to bring them down.

sentences.zh: 叔寶應命，躍馬負槍而進，必刺之萬眾之中，人馬辟易，太宗以是益重之，叔寶亦以此頗自矜尚。

translations.literal: Shubao answered the command, leapt his horse bearing lance and advanced, invariably stabbing them amid ten thousand men; men and horses gave way; Taizong therefore valued him more; Shubao also for this was somewhat self-admiring.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao would charge in, invariably killing them in the midst of the host; the prince prized him all the more, and Shubao grew somewhat proud of it.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，從誅建成、元吉。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month he followed in executing Jiancheng and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month he took part in killing Jiancheng and Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 事寧，拜左武衛大將軍，食實封七百戶。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was appointed Left Martial Guard Grand General with a substantive fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup he became left martial guard grand general with a substantive fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其後每多疾病，因謂人曰：「吾少長戎馬，所經二百餘陣，屢中重瘡。

translations.literal: Afterward he often had many illnesses; he therefore said to people: "I from youth grew up in war horses; the campaigns I passed through numbered more than two hundred; repeatedly I received grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was often ill and said: "I have fought in more than two hundred battles since youth and been gravely wounded many times.

sentences.zh: 計吾前後出血亦數斛矣，安得不病乎？」

translations.literal: Counting the blood I have shed before and after, it also amounts to several hu—how could I not be ill?
translations.idiomatic: I have lost several hu of blood in all—no wonder I am sick.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，贈徐州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died; posthumously enfeoffed as Military Governor of Xuzhou and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 12 and was buried at Zhaoling with posthumous rank as military governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗特令所司就其塋內立石人馬，以旌戰陣之功焉。

translations.literal: Taizong specially ordered the relevant office to erect stone men and horses at his tomb mound to proclaim achievements in battle arrays.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered stone men and horses erected at his tomb to commemorate his battlefield deeds.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改封胡國公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year his fief was changed to Duke of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 his title was changed to Duke of Hu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，與長孫無忌等圖形於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he and Zhangsun Wuji and others had their portraits at Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 his portrait was painted at Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 程知節，本名咬金，濟州東阿人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Zhijie, original personal name Yaojin, was a native of Dong'e in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Zhijie, originally named Yaojin, came from Dong'e in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 少驍勇，善用馬槊。

translations.literal: In youth he was fierce and brave, skilled in using the mounted lance.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was fierce and skilled with the cavalry lance.

sentences.zh: 大業末，聚徒數百，共保鄉里，以備他盜。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he gathered several hundred followers, together protecting the village against other bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Sui he gathered several hundred men to defend his home district.

sentences.zh: 後依李密，署為內軍驃騎。

translations.literal: Later he attached to Li Mi and was appointed as Inner Army Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Li Mi and became a flying-cavalry officer of the inner army.

sentences.zh: 時密於軍中簡勇士尤異者八千人，隸四驃騎，分為左右以自衛，號為內軍。

translations.literal: At the time Mi in the army selected eight thousand warriors of exceptional valor as the four Flying Cavalry, divided into left and right to guard himself, called the Inner Army.
translations.idiomatic: Mi chose eight thousand of his bravest men for four flying-cavalry units, left and right, as his personal guard—the inner army.

sentences.zh: 自云：「此八千人可當百萬。」

translations.literal: He himself said: "These eight thousand men can match a million.
translations.idiomatic: He boasted: "These eight thousand can match a million.

sentences.zh: 知節既領其一，甚被恩遇。

translations.literal: Zhijie then commanded one of them and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie commanded one unit and was highly favored.

sentences.zh: 及王世充出城決戰，知節領內馬軍，與密同營在北邙山上，單雄信領外馬軍，營在偃師城北。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong came out of the city for a decisive battle, Zhijie commanded the inner horse army; with Mi he encamped together on Mount Beimang; Shan Xiongxin commanded the outer horse army, encamped north of Yanshi city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong offered battle outside the city, Zhijie led the inner cavalry and camped with Mi on Mount Beimang while Shan Xiongxin camped north of Yanshi with the outer cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世充來襲雄信營，密遣知節及裴行儼助之。

translations.literal: Shichong came to raid Xiongxin's camp; Mi sent Zhijie and Pei Xingyan to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong attacked Xiongxin's camp; Mi sent Zhijie and Pei Xingyan to help.

sentences.zh: 行儼先馳赴敵，為流矢所中，墜於地。

translations.literal: Xingyan first galloped to meet the enemy and was struck by a stray arrow, falling to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyan charged first, was hit by a stray arrow, and fell.

sentences.zh: 知節救之，殺數人，世充軍披靡，乃抱行儼重騎而還。

translations.literal: Zhijie rescued him, killed several men; Shichong's army scattered; he then embraced Xingyan, remounted, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie rescued him, killed several men, scattered Wang's troops, lifted Xingyan back onto his horse, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 為世充騎所逐，刺槊洞過，知節回身捩折其槊，兼斬獲追者，於是與行儼俱免。

translations.literal: Pursued by Shichong's cavalry, a thrusting lance pierced through; Zhijie turned and wrenched the lance broken, also cutting down those who pursued; thus he and Xingyan both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's horsemen pursued; a lance pierced through him; Zhijie turned, broke the lance, killed his pursuers, and both escaped.

sentences.zh: 及密敗，世充得之，接遇甚厚。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, Shichong obtained him and received him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: After Mi's defeat Wang Shichong took him in and treated him well.

sentences.zh: 知節謂秦叔寶曰：「世充器度淺狹，而多妄語，好為咒誓，乃巫師老嫗耳，豈是撥亂主乎？」

translations.literal: Zhijie said to Qin Shubao: "Shichong's breadth of mind is shallow and narrow, and he has much false speech; he loves to make curses and oaths—he is but an old witch; how could he be a lord who settles turmoil?
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie told Qin Shubao: "Shichong is narrow-minded, full of empty talk and oaths like an old witch—how could he be a ruler who ends chaos?

sentences.zh: 及世充拒王師於九曲，知節領兵在其陣，與秦叔寶等馬上揖世充曰：「荷公接待，極欲報恩。

translations.literal: When Shichong resisted the imperial army at Jiugqu, Zhijie commanded troops in his formation; with Qin Shubao and others on horseback they bowed to Shichong: "We owe Your Grace reception and greatly wish to repay favor.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiugqu, with Shubao and others, Zhijie bowed from horseback and said: "You have treated us well and we wished to repay you—

sentences.zh: 公性猜貳，傍多扇惑，非僕託身之所，今謹奉辭。」

translations.literal: Your nature is suspicious and divided, with many beside you stirring confusion—this is not where I entrust my person; I now respectfully take leave."
translations.idiomatic: but you are suspicious and easily swayed; this is no place for us—we take our leave.

sentences.zh: 於是躍馬與左右數十人歸國，世充懼，不敢追之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they spurred their horses and with several tens on left and right returned to the state; Shichong was afraid and did not dare pursue.
translations.idiomatic: They galloped off with several dozen men to the Tang; Shichong feared to pursue.

sentences.zh: 授秦王府左三統軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Third Commander of the Prince of Qin's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: He became left third commander of the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 破宋金剛，擒竇建德，降王世充，並領左一馬軍總管。

translations.literal: Defeating Song Jingang, capturing Dou Jiande, and reducing Wang Shichong, he also held the post of Left First Cavalry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Song Jingang, captured Dou Jiande, and helped reduce Wang Shichong, serving as left first cavalry commander.

sentences.zh: 每陣先登，以功封宿國公。

translations.literal: In every battle he took the lead in the assault; for achievements he was enfeoffed as Duke of Su.
translations.idiomatic: He led every charge and was enfeoffed as Duke of Su.

sentences.zh: 武德七年，建成忌之，構之於高祖，除康州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wude, Jiancheng resented him; he framed him before Gaozu, and he was removed to Prefect of Kangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 7 Jiancheng slandered him to Gaozu and he was banished to Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 知節白太宗曰：「大王手臂今並翦除，身必不久。

translations.literal: Zhijie told Taizong plainly: "The King's arms are now all cut away; your person cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: He told the prince: "Your brothers have cut away your arms; you cannot last.

sentences.zh: 知節以死不去，願速自全。」

translations.literal: Zhijie would not leave even at death and urged swift self-preservation."
translations.idiomatic: He vowed to die rather than leave and urged the prince to save himself at once.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，從太宗討建成、元吉。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month he followed Taizong in punishing Jiancheng and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month he joined the prince in killing Jiancheng and Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 事定，拜太子右衛率，遷右武衛大將軍，賜實封七百戶。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was appointed Right Guard Commander of the Crown Prince, promoted to Right Martial Guard Grand General, granted a substantive fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup he became crown prince right guard commander, then right martial guard grand general, with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，歷瀘州都督、左領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan reign he served in succession as Military Governor of Luzhou and Left Leading Army Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he governed Luzhou and became left leading army grand general.

sentences.zh: 與長孫無忌等代襲刺史，改封盧國公，授普州刺史。

translations.literal: With Zhangsun Wuji and others he received hereditary prefectships; his fief was changed to Duke of Lu and he was appointed Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He was among the hereditary prefects and was made Duke of Lu and prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 十七年，累轉左屯衛大將軍，檢校北門屯兵，加鎮軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was repeatedly transferred to Left Tunwei Grand General, inspected the northern gate garrison troops, and added Grand General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he became left tunwei grand general, inspector of the northern gate garrison, and grand general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 永徽六年，遷左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui he was transferred to Left Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 6 he became left guard grand general.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，授蔥山道行軍大總管以討賀魯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was appointed Commander on Campaign of the Congshan Circuit to punish Helu.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 2 he commanded the Congshan circuit campaign against Helu.

sentences.zh: 師次怛篤城，有胡人數千家開門出降，知節屠城而去，賀魯遂即遠遁。

translations.literal: The army halted at Dudu City; several thousand households of Hu opened the gates and surrendered; Zhijie slaughtered the city and left; Helu thereupon fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: At Dudu City thousands of Hu surrendered; Zhijie massacred the city and Helu fled.

sentences.zh: 軍還，坐免官。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was removed from office for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was dismissed for the massacre.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 表請乞骸骨，許之。

translations.literal: He memorialized begging to retire; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to retire and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年卒，贈驃騎大將軍、益州大都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Linde he died; posthumously enfeoffed as Flying Cavalry Grand General and Grand Protector-General of Yizhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Linde 2 and was buried at Zhaoling with posthumous rank as flying-cavalry grand general and grand protector-general of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 子處默，襲爵盧國公。

translations.literal: His son Chumo inherited the Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chumo inherited the dukedom of Lu.

sentences.zh: 處亮，以功臣子尚太宗女清河長公主，授駙馬都尉、左衛中郎將。

translations.literal: Chuliang, as son of a meritorious minister, married Emperor Taizong's daughter Princess Changhe of Qinghe, was appointed Commandant of the Horse and left guard middle general.
translations.idiomatic: Chuliang married Princess Changhe and became commandant of the horse and left guard middle general.

sentences.zh: 少子處弼，官至右金吾將軍。

translations.literal: The youngest son Chubi reached the office of Right Golden Raven General.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Chubi rose to right golden raven general.

sentences.zh: 處弼子伯獻，開元中，左金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Chubi's son Boxian, in the Kaiyuan reign, was Left Golden Raven Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Chubi's son Boxian was left golden raven grand general under Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 段志玄，齊州臨淄人也。

translations.literal: Duan Zhixuan was a native of Linzi in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhixuan came from Linzi in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 父偃師，隋末為太原郡司法書佐，從高祖起義，官至郢州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yanshi in late Sui was judicial clerk of Taiyuan commandery; he followed Gaozu in raising righteousness and reached the office of Prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanshi, a Taiyuan judicial clerk in late Sui, followed Gaozu in the uprising and became prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 志玄從父在太原，甚為太宗所接待。

translations.literal: Zhixuan followed his father at Taiyuan and was greatly received by Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father to Taiyuan and won the prince's favor.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，志玄募得千餘人，授右領大都督府軍頭。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Zhixuan recruited more than a thousand men and was appointed Army Head of the Right Leading Grand Protector-General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the uprising he raised over a thousand men and became an army head in the right leading office.

sentences.zh: 從平霍邑，下絳郡，攻永豐倉，皆為先鋒，歷遷左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following in the pacification of Huoyi, taking Jiang commandery, and attacking the Yongfeng granary, he was always vanguard and was repeatedly promoted to Left Glory Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was vanguard at Huoyi, Jiang, and Yongfeng granary and rose to left glory grand master.

sentences.zh: 從劉文靜拒屈突通於潼關，文靜為通將桑顯和所襲，軍營已潰，志玄率二十騎赴擊，殺數十人而還。

translations.literal: Following Liu Wenjing in resisting Qu Tuotong at Tong Pass, when Wenjing was struck by Tong's general Sang Xianhe, the army camp was already routed; Zhixuan led twenty riders to strike, killed several tens, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass, when Liu Wenjing's camp collapsed under Sang Xianhe, Zhixuan charged with twenty riders, killed dozens, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 為流矢中足，慮眾心動，忍而不言，更入賊陣者再三。

translations.literal: Struck by a stray arrow in the foot, fearing the masses' hearts would stir, he endured without speaking and entered the rebel formation again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Shot in the foot, he hid the wound and charged the enemy lines repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 顯和軍亂，大軍因此復振，擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xianhe's army fell into disorder; the great army thereby revived and struck, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy line broke; the Tang army rallied and routed them.

sentences.zh: 及屈突通之遁，志玄與諸將追而擒之，以功授樂游府驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Qu Tuotong fled, Zhixuan with the generals pursued and captured him; for merit he was appointed Flying Cavalry General of Leyou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He helped capture Qu Tuotong and was made flying-cavalry general of Leyou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後從討王世充，深入陷陣，馬倒，為賊所擒。

translations.literal: Later following the campaign against Wang Shichong, he pressed deep into the formation; his horse fell and he was captured by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Wang Shichong, he was thrown and captured when his horse fell.

sentences.zh: 兩騎夾持其髻，將渡洛水，志玄踴身而奮，二人俱墜馬，馳歸，追者數百騎，不敢逼。

translations.literal: Two riders held his topknot and were about to cross the Luo River; Zhixuan leapt and struggled; both fell from their horses; he galloped back; several hundred pursuing riders did not dare press.
translations.idiomatic: Two rebels seized his hair to drag him across the Luo; he fought free, both fell, he escaped, and hundreds of pursuers dared not close.

sentences.zh: 及破竇建德，平東都，功又居多。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande was defeated and the Eastern Capital pacified, his achievements again ranked the most.
translations.idiomatic: He won top credit in the defeats of Dou Jiande and Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 遷秦王府右二護軍，賞物二千段。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Second Protector-General of the Prince of Qin's mansion, rewarded with two thousand lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He became right second protector-general of the Qin mansion with two thousand lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 隱太子建成、巢剌王元吉競以金帛誘之，志玄拒而不納，密以白太宗，竟與尉遲敬德等同誅建成、元吉。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng and Nest-stinging Prince Yuanji both competed to entice him with gold and silk; Zhixuan refused and did not accept, secretly reporting to Taizong; in the end with Yuchi Jingde and others alike he executed Jiancheng and Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji tried to buy him with gold; he refused and warned the prince, then joined Jingde in killing them.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，累遷左驍衛大將軍，封樊國公，食實封九百戶。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne he was repeatedly promoted to Left Xiaoqi Grand General, enfeoffed as Duke of Fan, with a substantive fief of nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the prince's accession he became left xiaoqi grand general, Duke of Fan, with nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后之葬也，志玄與宇文士及分統士馬出肅章門。

translations.literal: At the burial of Empress Wende, Zhixuan with Yuwen Shiji divided command of troops and horses out through Suxiang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Wende's funeral he and Yuwen Shiji commanded troops leaving Suxiang Gate.

sentences.zh: 太宗夜使宮官至二將軍所，士及開營內使者，志玄閉門不納，曰：「軍門不可夜開。」

translations.literal: Taizong at night sent a palace official to the two generals' posts; Shiji opened the camp to the inner envoy; Zhixuan closed the gate and would not admit him, saying: "The army gate cannot be opened at night.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a night messenger; Shiji admitted him but Zhixuan barred the gate: "The camp gate does not open at night.

sentences.zh: 使者曰：「此有手敕。」

translations.literal: The envoy said: "Here is a handwritten edict.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy said he bore an imperial order.

sentences.zh: 志玄曰：「夜中不辯真偽。」

translations.literal: Zhixuan said: "In the night one cannot distinguish true from false."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixuan replied: "At night one cannot tell real from false."

sentences.zh: 竟停使者至曉。

translations.literal: He finally detained the envoy until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: He held the envoy until dawn.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而嘆曰：「此真將軍也，周亞夫無以加焉。」

translations.literal: Taizong heard and sighed: "This is a true general; Zhou Yafu cannot surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him: "A true general—Zhou Yafu was no better.

sentences.zh: 十一年，定世封之制，授金州刺史，改封褒國公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the system of hereditary enfeoffments for the age was fixed; he was appointed Prefect of Jinzhou and his fief changed to Duke of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was made hereditary prefect of Jinzhou and Duke of Bao.

sentences.zh: 十二年，拜右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Right Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he became right guard grand general.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加鎮軍大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was added Grand General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was made grand general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 十六年，寢疾，太宗親自臨視，涕泣而別，顧謂曰：「當與卿子五品。」

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he lay ill; Taizong personally came to visit, wept in parting, and turning said: "I shall give your son fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16, gravely ill, he was visited by the weeping emperor, who promised fifth rank for his son.

sentences.zh: 志玄頓首固請回授母弟志感，太宗遂授志感左衛郎將。

translations.literal: Zhixuan kowtowed and firmly asked to transfer it to his mother's younger brother Zhigan; Taizong thereupon appointed Zhigan Left Guard Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the rank go to his uncle Zhigan instead, and the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上為發哀，哭之甚慟，贈輔國將軍、揚州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰忠壯。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor held mourning, wept very bitterly, posthumously enfeoffed him as General Who Assists the State and Military Governor of Yangzhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling, posthumous name Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the emperor mourned deeply, enfeoffed him posthumously as general who assists the state and military governor of Yangzhou with the name Loyal and Strong, and buried him at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月，詔圖形於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year an edict ordered his portrait at Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 17 his portrait joined Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 子瓚，襲爵褒國公，武太后時，官至左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His son Zan inherited the Duke of Bao; in Empress Wu's time he reached Left Tunwei Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zan inherited the dukedom and rose to left tunwei grand general under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 子懷簡，襲爵，開元中，官至太子詹事。

translations.literal: His son Huaijian inherited the fief; in the Kaiyuan reign he reached Crown Prince Household Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaijian inherited and became crown prince household minister under Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 張公謹，字弘慎，魏州繁水人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongjin, style Hongshen, was a native of Fanshui in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongjin, courtesy name Hongshen, came from Fanshui in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 初為王世充洧州長史。

translations.literal: Initially he was Chief Administrator of Wei prefecture under Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Wang Shichong as chief administrator of Wei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，與王世充所署洧州刺史崔樞以州城歸國，授鄒州別駕，累除右武候長史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, with Cui Shu, whom Shichong had appointed Prefect of Wei, he surrendered the prefectural city to the state; he was appointed Vice Prefect of Zou, repeatedly promoted to Chief of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 he and Cui Shu surrendered Wei to the Tang; he became vice prefect of Zou and rose to chief of the right martial guard.

sentences.zh: 初未知名，李勣尉遲敬德亦言之，乃引入幕府。

translations.literal: At first he was not yet known by name; Li Jiji and Yuchi Jingde also spoke of him, and he was then brought into the staff headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiji and Yuchi Jingde recommended him and he entered the prince's staff.

sentences.zh: 時太宗為隱太子建成、巢王元吉所忌，因召公謹，問以自安之策，對甚合旨，漸見親遇。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong was resented by the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng and Prince of Qi Yuanji; he therefore summoned Gongjin and asked strategies for self-preservation; the replies very much matched his intent and he was gradually seen with intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiancheng and Yuanji threatened him, he asked Gongjin for counsel; the answers pleased him and he grew intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 及太宗將討建成、元吉，遣卜者灼龜佔之，公謹自外來見，遽投於地而進曰：「凡卜筮者，將以決嫌疑，定猶豫，今既事在不疑，何卜之有？
