translations.literal: When Taizong was about to punish Jiancheng and Yuanji, he sent a diviner to burn turtle and divine; Gongjin coming from outside saw this, hastily cast it to the ground and advanced: "All divination is to decide doubt and settle hesitation; now the affair is beyond doubt—why divine?
translations.idiomatic: As the prince prepared to strike, a diviner was burning turtle shells; Gongjin threw them down and said: "Divination resolves doubt—there is no doubt here; why divine?

sentences.zh: 縱卜之不吉，勢不可已。

translations.literal: Even if divination were inauspicious, the momentum cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the omen were bad, you cannot stop now.

sentences.zh: 願大王思之。」

translations.literal: I wish the Great King to think on this.
translations.idiomatic: Think on it, my lord.

sentences.zh: 太宗深然其言。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was deeply convinced.

sentences.zh: 六月四日，公謹與長孫無忌等九人伏於玄武門以俟變。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the sixth month Gongjin with Zhangsun Wuji and nine others lay in ambush at Xuanwu Gate awaiting the change.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the sixth month he waited at Xuanwu Gate with Zhangsun Wuji and eight others.

sentences.zh: 及斬建成、元吉，其黨來攻玄武門，兵鋒甚盛。

translations.literal: When Jiancheng and Yuanji were beheaded, their faction came to attack Xuanwu Gate; the blades of war were very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes were killed, their followers assaulted Xuanwu Gate fiercely.

sentences.zh: 公謹有勇力，獨閉門以拒之。

translations.literal: Gongjin had courage and strength; alone he closed the gate to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Gongjin alone barred the gate and held them off.

sentences.zh: 以功累授左武候將軍，封定遠郡公，賜實封一千戶。

translations.literal: For achievements he was repeatedly appointed Left Martial Guard General, enfeoffed as Duke of Dingyuan commandery, granted a substantive fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left martial guard general, Duke of Dingyuan, with a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，拜代州都督，上表請置屯田以省轉運，又前後言時政得失十餘事，並見納用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed Military Governor of Daizhou; he memorialized asking to establish garrison farming to save transport costs, and also spoke more than ten times on gains and losses of current policy before and after—all were accepted and used.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 he governed Daizhou, proposed garrison farming to cut transport costs, and offered more than ten policy critiques—all adopted.

sentences.zh: 後遣李靖經略突厥，以公謹為副，公謹因言突厥可取之狀曰：「頡利縱慾肆情，窮凶極暴，誅害良善，暱近小人，此主昏於上，其可取一也。

translations.literal: Later Li Jing strategized against the Turks; Gongjin was his deputy; Gongjin therefore stated the condition in which Turks could be taken: "Jieli indulges desires and acts wantonly, to the utmost cruel and violent, executing and harming the good, favoring petty men close at hand—this lord is muddled above; he can be taken for reason one.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Jing's deputy against the Turks, he argued they could be taken because Jieli was tyrannical and muddled at the top—reason one.

sentences.zh: 又其別部同羅、僕骨、回紇、延陀之類，並自立君長，將圖反噬，此則眾叛於下，其可取二也。

translations.literal: Moreover his separate tribes Tongluo, Pugu, Huihe, Yantuo, and the like each set up their own lords and chiefs, about to turn and bite back—this is the masses rebelling below; he can be taken for reason two.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribes Tongluo, Pugu, Huihe, and Yantuo were setting up rival chiefs ready to rebel—reason two.

sentences.zh: 突厥被疑，輕騎自免；

translations.literal: The Turks are suspected; light cavalry escape on their own;
translations.idiomatic: Turk leaders fled in suspicion on light horses;

sentences.zh: 拓設出討，匹馬不歸；

translations.literal: the Tuo she went out on campaign and not one horse returned;
translations.idiomatic: the Tuo she campaign lost every horse;

sentences.zh: 欲谷喪師，立足無地，此則兵挫將敗，其可取三也。

translations.literal: Yugu lost his army and had no ground to stand on—this is troops defeated and generals broken; he can be taken for reason three.
translations.idiomatic: Yugu lost his army and had nowhere to stand—reason three.

sentences.zh: 塞北霜早，糧餱乏絕，其可取四也。

translations.literal: North of the passes frost came early and grain rations were cut off; he can be taken for reason four.
translations.idiomatic: Early frost and famine in the north—reason four.

sentences.zh: 頡利疏其突厥，親委諸胡，胡人翻覆，是其常性，大軍一臨，內必生變，其可取五也。

translations.literal: Jieli estranged his Turks and personally entrusted various Hu; the Hu are treacherous and that is their constant nature—when the great army arrives, within they will surely change; he can be taken for reason five.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli favored the Hu, who are treacherous by nature and would turn when the Tang army came—reason five.

sentences.zh: 華人入北，其類實多，比聞自相嘯聚，保據山險，師出塞垣，自然有應，其可取六也。」

translations.literal: Chinese entering the north are very many in kind; recently heard they gather and roar among themselves, hold mountain passes and danger—when the army leaves the border wall, naturally there will be response; he can be taken for reason six.
translations.idiomatic: Many Chinese in the north would rise when the army crossed the border—reason six.

sentences.zh: 太宗深納之。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted every point.

sentences.zh: 破定襄，敗頡利，璽書慰勞，進封鄒國公。

translations.literal: Breaking Dingxiang and defeating Jieli, imperial writing comforted and rewarded him; he was advanced to Duke of Zou.
translations.idiomatic: After Dingxiang and Jieli fell, he was advanced to Duke of Zou.

sentences.zh: 轉襄州都督，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: Transferred to Military Governor of Xiangzhou, he had very benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: As military governor of Xiangzhou he ruled with notable kindness.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年三十九。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而嗟悼，出次發哀，有司奏言：「准《陰陽書》，日子在辰，不可哭泣，又為流俗所忌。」

translations.literal: Taizong heard and sighed in grief; he went out to halt and hold mourning; the relevant office memorialized: "According to the Book of Yin and Yang, on days when the son is in chen one cannot weep; it is also tabooed by floating custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him; officials cited the almanac forbidding tears when the son was in chen.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「君臣之義，同於父子，情發於衷，安避辰日？」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "The righteousness of ruler and minister is the same as father and son; feeling issues from the breast—how avoid the day of chen?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Between ruler and minister and father and son, grief comes from the heart—why obey the almanac?

sentences.zh: 遂哭之。

translations.literal: He then wept.
translations.idiomatic: And he wept.

sentences.zh: 贈左驍衛大將軍，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Left Xiaoqi Grand General, posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left xiaoqi grand general with the name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，追思舊功，改封郯國公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, recalling old achievements, his fief was changed to Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 his title was changed to Duke of Tan in remembrance of his service.

sentences.zh: 十七年，圖形於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year his portrait was at Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 his portrait was painted at Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，又贈荊州都督。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui reign he was again posthumously enfeoffed as Military Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yonghui he was posthumously made military governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 長子大象嗣，官至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: The eldest son Daxiang inherited, reaching Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Daxiang inherited and rose to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 次子大素、大安，並知名。

translations.literal: The second sons Dasu and Da'an were both well known.
translations.idiomatic: His second sons Dasu and Da'an were both famous.

sentences.zh: 大素，龍朔中歷位東台舍人，兼修國史，卒於懷州長史，撰《後魏書》一百卷、《隋書》三十捲。

translations.literal: Dasu in the Longshuo reign held office as Eastern Terrace Attendant, also editing the national history; he died as Chief Administrator of Huaizhou, compiling the Book of Later Wei in one hundred juan and the Book of Sui in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Dasu served on the eastern terrace and edited the histories, compiling the Book of Later Wei in 100 juan and the Book of Sui in 30 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 大安，上元中歷太子庶子、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: Da'an in the Shangyuan reign held office as Crown Prince Household Subordinate and Tong Zhongshu Menxia Sanpin.
translations.idiomatic: Da'an was crown prince household subordinate and co-director of the Secretariat under Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 時章懷太子在春宮，令大安與太子洗馬劉訥言等注范曄《後漢書》。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Zhanghuai was in the Eastern Palace; he ordered Da'an with Crown Prince Study Companion Liu Nayan and others to annotate Fan Ye's Book of Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: For Prince Zhanghuai he annotated Fan Ye's Book of Later Han with Liu Nayan and others.

sentences.zh: 宮廢，左授普州刺史。

translations.literal: When the palace was abolished, he was demoted left to Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern palace fell he was demoted to prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 光宅中，卒於橫州司馬。

translations.literal: In the Guangzhai reign he died as Administrator of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as administrator of Hengzhou under Guangzhai.

sentences.zh: 大安子涚，開元中為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Da'an's son Shuang, in the Kaiyuan reign, was Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Da'an's son Shuang was chancellor of the directorate of education under Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：敬德奪槊陷陣，鼓勇王師，卻賂報恩，竭忠霸主。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Jingde seized lances and broke formations, rousing courage in the King's army, refusing bribes and repaying favor, exhausting loyalty to the hegemon lord.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Jingde seized lances, broke enemy lines, refused bribes, and served his lord with utter loyalty.

sentences.zh: 然而奮拳負氣，非自全之道；

translations.literal: Yet striking with fists and relying on spirit was not the way of self-preservation;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his proud temper was no way to preserve himself;

sentences.zh: 文皇告誡之言，可為功臣藥石。

translations.literal: Wen Huang's admonishing words can serve as medicine and stone for meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's warning to him should be medicine for every meritorious minister.

sentences.zh: 叔寶善用馬槊，拔賊壘則以寡敵眾，可謂勇矣。

translations.literal: Shubao was skilled in using the mounted lance; pulling rebel ramparts he with few opposed many—this can be called brave.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao mastered the lance and with few men stormed enemy walls—that was true courage.

sentences.zh: 知節志平國難，拜隼籞則致命輔君，可謂忠矣。

translations.literal: Zhijie aspired to pacify the state's hardship; bowing at the falcon-perch office he gave his life to assist the lord—this can be called loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijie sought to end the realm's crisis and, once in imperial service, gave his life to his sovereign—truly loyal.

sentences.zh: 而並曉世充之猜貳，識唐代之霸圖，可謂見幾君子矣。

translations.literal: Moreover both understood Shichong's suspicion and division and recognized the Tang age's hegemonic design—this can be called gentlemen who see the first signs.
translations.idiomatic: Both saw through Wang Shichong's deceit and recognized the Tang's destiny—men who read the times aright.

sentences.zh: 志玄中鏑不言，竟安師旅。

translations.literal: Zhixuan was struck by an arrowhead yet did not speak, and in the end secured the army brigades.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixuan took an arrow in silence and thereby steadied the army.

sentences.zh: 公謹投龜定議，志助儲君。

translations.literal: Gongjin cast aside the turtle and settled the plan, his will set on assisting the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Gongjin cast aside divination to fix the coup and devoted himself to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 皆所謂猛將謀臣，知機識變。

translations.literal: All are what are called fierce generals and plotting ministers, knowing the moment and recognizing change.
translations.idiomatic: All were fierce generals and shrewd advisers who grasped the moment and adapted to change.

sentences.zh: 有唐之盛，斯實賴焉。

translations.literal: The Tang's flourishing truly relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: The greatness of Tang owed much to men such as these.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：太宗經綸，實賴虎臣。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Taizong's weaving of the realm truly relied on tiger ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Taizong's founding of the empire rested on tiger-like champions.

sentences.zh: 胡、鄂諸將，奮不顧身。

translations.literal: The generals of Hu and E and the rest strove without regard for their persons.
translations.idiomatic: The dukes of Hu and E and their peers fought without thought for their lives.

sentences.zh: 圖形凌煙，配食嚴禋。

translations.literal: Their portraits were painted at Lingyan; they received sacrificial shares in the solemn suburban sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Their faces were painted at Lingyan Pavilion; they shared in the grand state sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 光諸簡冊，為報君親。

translations.literal: They glorify the various bamboo slips and registers, repaying ruler and kin.
translations.idiomatic: Their glory shines in the histories as repayment to sovereign and father.
